recalls.Description: This recall involves CHE-US magnetic stick figure toys. The robot-shaped toys were sold in sets of five or 10 purple, blue, yellow, red and green stick figures. Each stick figure has four small magnets, one in each hand and foot. “X004N3MGCB” is printed on the back of the product packaging.
recalls.Title: CHE-US Recalls Magnetic Robot Toys Due to Risk of Serious Injury or Death from Magnet Ingestion; Violate Mandatory Standard for Toys

Images.Caption: Recalled CHE-US Magnetic Robot Stick Figures
“X004N3MGCB” is printed on the back of the CHE-US magnetic robot stick figures’ product packaging.

Retailers.Name:
Sold Online At:
Amazon.com from April 2025 through August 2026 for between t $9 and $18.
Guangzhou Shian Trading Co., Ltd., dba CHE-US/CHESLICR, of China.

Hazards.Name: The recalled magnetic stick figures violate the mandatory standard for toys because when pulled apart, the figures’ arms and legs liberate high-powered magnets posing an ingestion hazard to children. When high-powered magnets are swallowed, the ingested magnets can attract each other, or other metal objects, and become lodged in the digestive system. This can result in perforations, twisting, and/or blockage of the intestines, blood poisoning and death.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should stop using the stick figures immediately, take them away from children and contact CHE-US for a full refund. Consumers will be asked to send a photo of the toys in the trash to CHE-USMagneticRobotToysRecall@outlook.com. Consumers should then dispose of the recalled product.

recalls.Description: This recall involves Cipton-branded bicycle helmets. They were sold in white and in youth size small (S), fitting a head circumference of about 19.7 to 21.3 inches. The helmets have black padding, black straps, black buckle and a built-in, multi-colored LED light strip. Model “CPSK300CC” is printed on a label on the inside of the helmet.
recalls.Title: Cipton Recalls Bicycle Helmets Due to Risk of Serious Injury or Death from Head Injury; Violate Mandatory Standard for Bicycle Helmets
recalls.ConsumerContact: Cipton at 888-588-1629 from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. ET Monday through Friday, email at Reply@customersupport123.com, or online at Southerntelecom.com/recall-2026-11-19 or Southerntelecom.com and click “Recall” at the top of the page for more information.

Model “CPSK300CC” is printed on a label inside the recalled Cipton helmets.

Retailers.Name:
Sold At:
Dicks Sporting Goods and JC Penny nationwide and online at Dickssportinggoods.com from April 2024 through May 2026 for about $35.

Distributors.Name: Hardline Group, dba Cipton, of Brooklyn, New York

Hazards.Name: The recalled helmets violate the mandatory safety standard for bicycle helmets because the helmets do not comply with the impact attenuation, positional stability and certification requirements. The helmets can fail to protect the user in the event of a crash, posing a serious risk of injury or death due to head injury.

Remedies.Name:
Consumers should stop using the helmets immediately and contact Cipton for a full refund. Consumers will be asked to destroy the helmet by cutting the straps and writing in permanent marker “Recalled” on the helmet and send a photo of the destroyed helmet to Reply@customersupport123.com. Consumers should then dispose of the recalled product.

Hazards.Name: The various trade tools violate the mandatory safety standard for consumer products with button cell and coin batteries because the button batteries can be accessed easily by children, posing an ingestion hazard. recalls.Description:
Washington, D.C. -- The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) and Guangzhouyupinkejiyouxiangongsi (Guangzhou Yupin Technology Co., Ltd) dba Xentrawave, of China, are announcing the recall of the Xentrawave adult portable bed rails, models XT016 (all batches) and XT026 (batch number 20251212).  

The adult portable bed rails fail to meet mandatory standard requirements, because users can become entrapped within the bed rail or between the bed rail and the side of the mattress, posing a serious entrapment hazard and risk of death by asphyxiation. In addition, the XT016 model adult bed rail does not meet structural stability or retention strap requirements, posing entrapment hazards, and its push pins and push pin holes are incorrectly sized, posing a laceration hazard.  

CPSC has received one report of a death involving the Xentrawave adult portable bed rail, model XT016. In 2026, an 89-year-old woman died from asphyxiation after she became entrapped between the bed rail and mattress.   

About 2,114 adult portable bed rails were sold in the United States.  

The recalled bed rails were sold under the “Xentrawave” brand and under two model names, models “XT016” and “XT026”. The recall of the XT016 applies to all batch numbers, and the recall of XT026 model applies only to batch number “20251212”. The “Xentrawave” brand name is printed on a green label located on the bed rail’s grey fabric pouch. The model numbers “XT016” or “XT026” are located on the front of the product’s outer packaging and the first page of the instruction manual. The batch number “20251212” for the XT026 model is located on the product label attached to the back of the bed rail’s gray fabric pouch and in the instruction manual. The recalled bed rails have black or gray metal frames, gray foam rubber handle grips, and gray fabric pouches. The XT016 model measures about 12.2 inches wide by 25.5 inches high and the XT026 model measures about 12.2 inches wide by 21.5 inches high.  

The adult portable bed rails were sold by Xentrawave at Amazon.com. The XT016 bed rails were sold from May 2025 through March 2026 and the XT026 bed rails were sold from March 2026 through August 2026 for between $37 and $40.  


The adult portable bed rails were imported by Guangzhouyupinkejiyouxiangongsi (Guangzhou Yupin Technology Co., Ltd) dba Xentrawave, of China and manufactured by Guangzhou Nanyu Medical Technology Co., Ltd, of China.
